title: Submitting a Root Edit proposal requires 1% of circulating SKYBASE supply, waived only for buyback or grant proposals
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1 opens the Root Edit process with a stake gate: a proposal is submitted "through the Powerhouse system containing a draft Artifact Edit Proposal," and "a SKYBASE token holder must hold at least 1% of the circulating token supply to submit a proposal." It must also be posted publicly on the Sky Forum under the "Skybase Prime" category.

The exception is the interesting part. A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1 waives the 1% requirement "for proposals that solely entail a buyback or a grant of SKYBASE tokens," while stating that "all other procedural requirements within the Root Edit process continue to apply."

A submission threshold exists to suppress spam and force proposers to have skin in the game, but it also disenfranchises exactly the holders least able to coordinate 1% of supply. The carve-out concedes that for the one proposal class where small holders have the strongest legitimate interest — distributing value back to token holders — the gate does more harm than good.

The boundary is narrow and deliberately so: the proposal must *solely* entail a buyback or grant. Bundling a buyback with any other change re-imposes the 1% requirement, which blocks the obvious exploit of attaching unrelated edits to a threshold-exempt wrapper.
description: The waiver targets exactly the proposals a small holder would want to make — returning value to holders — while every other procedural requirement continues to apply.
